title: Constraint Theory Runtime — Eisenstein Snap Detection
content:
[KEY: Eisenstein snap] When two symmetric constraint regions collide at a critical threshold, the system exhibits a discrete phase transition called an Eisenstein snap.
[KEY: Detection method] Monitor the second derivative of the constraint gradient. A zero-crossing with magnitude > 2σ indicates a snap event.
[CROSS-REF: verification/phase-transitions.md]
[WARNING: False positives may occur near boundary conditions. Cross-reference with energy landscape analysis.]
[DOMAIN: constraint-theory] Core to string-theoretic constraint solving.
The snap frequency follows a Poisson distribution with λ proportional to constraint density. For optimal results, sample at 10× the Nyquist rate of the constraint manifold.

title: Fleet Ops — Vessel Deployment Pipeline
content:
[KEY: Vessel deployment] Each fleet agent runs as an independent vessel with isolated workspace and rootfs.
[KEY: Rolling update] Vessels are updated in waves of 3, with a 60-second cooldown between waves.
[CROSS-REF: fleet/orchestration.md]
[WARNING: Ensure at least 2 vessels remain healthy during any update wave.]
Deployment order: monitoring → workers → specialists. Rollback is automatic if health checks fail for >30s.
Status: 9/9 vessels healthy, last deployment at 2026-05-13T04:00Z.

content:
[KEY: Room taxonomy] PLATO rooms are organized by domain: forge/, fleet/, ops/, architecture/, research/.

title: Proof Forging Log — Toric Code Lattice Simplification
content:
[KEY: Toric code lattice] Simplified from 12×12 to 6×6 using constraint elimination on Z-stabilizers.
[KEY: Homology reduction] Reduced logical qubit count from 4 to 2 while preserving error correction distance d=3.
[CROSS-REF: forge/proofs/toric-code-base.md]
[DOMAIN: plato/forge/proofs]
Method: Perform Reidemeister-style moves on the constraint graph, merging vertices where stabilizers commute.
Result: 73% fewer edges, 58% fewer constraints, verification passes in 2.1s (was 18.4s).
Next step: Generalize to arbitrary surface codes with gen& parameter.

[CROSS-REF: fleet/i2i/pull-protocol.md]

Priority levels: low (informational), medium (needs action), high (blocking).

title: Research Log — Eisenstein Snap Frequency Analysis
content:
[KEY: Snap frequency] Measured snap frequency f = 0.037 snaps/s at constraint density ρ = 0.82.
[KEY: Density relationship] Snap frequency follows f ∝ ρ^2 * (1-ρ)^1.5 with R² = 0.994 for ρ in [0.1, 0.95].
[CROSS-REF: forge/constraints/eisenstein-snap-detection.md]
[DOMAIN: research/constraints]
Sampled 10,000 constraint configurations at 7 density levels. Confirmed Poisson arrival with λ = f * Δt.
Found resonant frequency at ρ ≈ 0.73 where successive snaps interfere constructively.
Practical implication: Avoid operating near ρ ≈ 0.73 for constraint solving; use ρ < 0.6 or ρ > 0.85 for stable behavior.
